key_insight: Fusing multi-scale foundation-model and FastVim features improved patch-level Gleason grading, rather than cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: More consistent automated Gleason grading could support prostate cancer risk assessment, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Combine frozen pathology foundation-model features with image features from a lightweight, distilled FastVim.
Encode both feature sources at multiple scales using Mamba state-space models.
Fuse encoded representations through a jointly trained classification head.
evidence_signal: On PANDA with 5-fold cross-validation, macro F1 reached 0.894 and Gleason pattern 5 F1 reached 0.802—reported relative gains of 12% and 21% over the best single-scale model.
watch_item: The abstract reports no external validation or prospective clinical evaluation, leaving real-world generalizability uncertain.
paper_title: Multi-scale Fusion of Fast Vision Mamba and Foundation Model Features for Patch-Level Gleason Grading in Computational Pathology
